text:
sara (customer): Hey team — our free trial credits dropped by ~12k tokens overnight. We didn’t run anything from the dashboard. Can someone check?

maria (support): Sorry to hear that, sara. Can you share your org id or billing id? Any recent promo code applied?

sara (customer): Org ID: org_9b7a. We did apply a promo last week but balance showed the credit. Checked the dashboard earlier and it was fine. Woke up to almost all gone.

maria (support): Thanks. I’m pulling usage logs. @alex can you look at background ingest jobs tied to that org?

alex (eng): On it. Quick scan shows a spike hitting embeddings endpoint from a worker pool labeled nightly-ingest-3 between 00:12–00:28 UTC. Job ids: ingest-9932, ingest-9933.

ingest-bot: retry event — ingest-9932 attempt 1 failed with 502, scheduled retry in 5s
ingest-bot: retry event — ingest-9932 attempt 2 succeeded, tokens: 7423
ingest-bot: retry event — ingest-9933 attempt 1 succeeded, tokens: 4835

mike_ops: Noting those token counts are large; why is attempt 1 of 9932 counted as failed but still charged on our end?

alex (eng): Looking at our billing attribution layer — we were counting token usage on request accept rather than final status for the streaming worker. If the worker retried, the first attempt still recorded usage.

maria (support): So duplicate charges from retries? That would explain the ~12k tokens. Does the promo exclude background jobs or auto-applies?

kevin (billing): Promo should apply to all eligible usage. But our credits deduction pipeline runs asynchronously and dedup is based on request_id; the ingest worker creates a new request_id for each retry.

alex (eng): Repro steps I ran: start a small reproduce with curl:

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-test-..." \
  -d '{"model":"embed-8k","input":"test"}'
```

Then I simulated a transient 502 from our edge and let the client retry once. In telemetry it produced two token records with different request_id but same job_id.

maria (support): Ok — root cause likely "retry creates new request_id -> double charge before deduping credits". Immediate actions?

alex (eng): Hotfix options: 1) change worker to preserve request_id across retries, 2) delay billing record until final status, 3) best-effort credit refund for affected orgs. I can implement (1) quickly and push a short-lived guard to the billing pipeline to ignore duplicate job_ids.

kevin (billing): For existing charge, we should offer a credit reversal for the duplicated token counts. I can prepare a manual reversal once eng confirms affected token delta per org.

maria (support): sara — we’ll escalate this as high priority. We’ll: (a) patch to stop future duplication, (b) reverse the duplicated tokens on your account, and (c) follow up with a postmortem. Sorry for the disruption.

sara (customer): Thanks. What’s ETA for the patch and reversal? My product team is panicking.

alex (eng): I’ll open a small PR to preserve request_id across retries — should be staged in ~40m and can be rolled to prod after smoke tests (~2h). I’ll also add a temporary filter in billing to ignore duplicate job_id tokens; that’s lower risk and I can ship in ~20m.

kevin (billing): I’ll queue the reversal once alex shares the token diff. Expect credit applied within 24 hours.

maria (support): Confirmed action items: alex -> patch + billing filter; kevin -> reversal; maria -> follow-up and PM sync. I’ll DM you updates, @sara.

sara (customer): Appreciate it. Please cc my CTO: @jordan.

maria (support): Will do.

alex (eng): Quick note — log snippet showing duplicate tokens (redacted):
```
[2026-03-16T00:12:03Z] job=ingest-9932 request_id=req_ab12 status=failed tokens_recorded=7423
[2026-03-16T00:12:09Z] job=ingest-9932 request_id=req_c3f4 status=success tokens_recorded=7423
```

mike_ops: Adding incident tag and setting priority P2.

maria (support): Updated ticket with P2, assigned to eng + billing. Will post postmortem link here when ready.

sara (customer): Thanks all.
